Find hits with a time-course model

Source: R/gene_level_statistics.R
find_time_hit.Rd

Finds the genes whose depletion (or enrichment) caused by the treatment grows over time, using a single model for the whole time course instead of a separate analysis for each time point. Both the treated and the untreated samples must cover at least two time points.

Usage

find_time_hit(
  screenR_Object,
  treatment,
  control,
  days,
  baseline = NULL,
  number_barcode = 3,
  direction = c("Down", "Up"),
  fdr = 0.05,
  fdr_method = c("BH", "storey"),
  time = NULL
)

Arguments

screenR_Object

The ScreenR object obtained using create_screenr_object, normalized with normalize_data. The model uses its raw counts with its effective library sizes as offsets, the same normalization as the plots and the data table (see create_edger_obj).

treatment

The value(s) of the Treatment column of get_sample_table for the treated samples.

control

The value(s) of the Treatment column of get_sample_table for the control samples.

days

The time points to use, in temporal order, as in the Day column of get_sample_table.

baseline

Optional value(s) of the Treatment column of samples taken before the treatment (for example the first time points), which are used as untreated samples.

number_barcode

Only genes with more than number_barcode barcodes are tested (default 3, so a gene needs at least 4 barcodes). The barcodes of a gene are tested together as a set, so this is not a number of barcodes that must change.

direction

"Down" (default) for genes depleted over time in the treated samples or "Up" for enriched genes.

fdr

The FDR threshold: only genes with an FDR lower than or equal to this value are returned (default 0.05). Use fdr = 1 to return all the genes with the given direction.

fdr_method

How the FDR is computed: "BH" (Benjamini-Hochberg, the default) or "storey" (Benjamini-Hochberg multiplied by the estimated proportion of genes without effect).

time

An optional named numeric vector with the real time of each time point of days (and of the days of the baseline samples), named by the values of the Day column, for example c(Time3 = 7, Time4 = 14). By default (NULL) the time points are numbered 0, 1, 2, ... in the order of days.

Value

A tibble with one row for each hit in the requested direction and the columns of camera (Gene, NGenes, Direction, PValue, FDR), where PValue is the one-sided p-value for the requested direction and FDR is computed from it, plus Log2FC: the median over the barcodes of the gene of c, the change of the treatment log2 fold change per time point (or per unit of time when time is given).

Details

The barcode counts are modelled with edgeR as log(abundance) = a + b * time + d * treated + c * time * treated, where time is the time of the sample and treated is 1 for the treated samples and 0 for the control and baseline samples. By default the time is the index of the time point (0 for the first element of days, 1 for the second, ...), so the time points are treated as equally spaced; give their real times with the time argument (for example days after selection) to fit the model against the actual time. The untreated samples and the treated samples each follow their own line; the coefficient c is the difference between the slopes, i.e. how much the treatment effect changes per time point. A constant treatment effect gives c = 0. The barcodes of each gene are then tested together with camera, as in find_camera_hit.

With real times, c (and the Log2FC column) is the change of the treatment log2 fold change per unit of time. With two time points the model is saturated: c is the difference between the treatment effects at the two time points divided by the time between them, so the p-values do not depend on the times. With three or more time points that are not equally spaced, the times matter: the model assumes that the treatment effect changes linearly with time, and real times fit that line against the actual time instead of the order of the samples. A treatment effect that does not change linearly (for example one that reaches a plateau) is not described well by this model.

See also

find_camera_hit, summarise_hits, plot_barcode_trend, get_sample_table

Examples

object <- get0("object", envir = asNamespace("ScreenR"))
get_sample_table(object)
#> # A tibble: 14 × 3
#>    Sample      Day   Treatment
#>    <chr>       <chr> <chr>    
#>  1 T1          T1    T1       
#>  2 T2          T2    T2       
#>  3 Time3_TRT_A Time3 TRT      
#>  4 Time3_TRT_B Time3 TRT      
#>  5 Time3_TRT_C Time3 TRT      
#>  6 Time3_A     Time3 Time3    
#>  7 Time3_B     Time3 Time3    
#>  8 Time3_C     Time3 Time3    
#>  9 Time4_TRT_A Time4 TRT      
#> 10 Time4_TRT_B Time4 TRT      
#> 11 Time4_TRT_C Time4 TRT      
#> 12 Time4_A     Time4 Time4    
#> 13 Time4_B     Time4 Time4    
#> 14 Time4_c     Time4 Time4    
find_time_hit(object,
    treatment = "TRT", control = c("Time3", "Time4"),
    days = c("Time3", "Time4"), fdr = 1
)
#> Warning: 3rows with all zero counts
#> Warning: Zero sample variances detected, have been offset away from zero
#> # A tibble: 258 × 6
#>    Gene     NGenes Direction   PValue   FDR Log2FC
#>    <chr>     <dbl> <fct>        <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl>
#>  1 Gene_296     10 Down      0.000661 0.336 -0.676
#>  2 Gene_372     12 Down      0.00166  0.336 -0.729
#>  3 Gene_422     10 Down      0.00189  0.336 -0.473
#>  4 Gene_87      10 Down      0.00568  0.510 -0.412
#>  5 Gene_412     10 Down      0.00572  0.510 -0.569
#>  6 Gene_419     10 Down      0.00573  0.510 -0.582
#>  7 Gene_349     10 Down      0.00705  0.538 -0.270
#>  8 Gene_292     10 Down      0.00929  0.544 -0.327
#>  9 Gene_370     10 Down      0.00973  0.544 -0.282
#> 10 Gene_325     10 Down      0.0102   0.544 -0.231
#> # ℹ 248 more rows

# With the real times (days after selection): with two time points the
# p-values are the same, and Log2FC is per day
find_time_hit(object,
    treatment = "TRT", control = c("Time3", "Time4"),
    days = c("Time3", "Time4"), time = c(Time3 = 7, Time4 = 14), fdr = 1
)
